awards.bar_to_the_dfc: Another round of hard flying that stood out. You’ve made danger a habit—and lived through it.
awards.bar_to_the_dfm: They’re saying you did it again. Same sky, same risk—more proof you don’t quit.
awards.bar_to_the_dso: A second time they credit your command in combat. You’ve carried responsibility where it hurts.
awards.bar_to_the_vc: A second VC is almost myth. It means you faced the impossible twice and refused to yield.
awards.distinguished_flying_cross_dfc: Gallantry in the air, the kind that holds a formation together. The ribbon looks clean; the sorties weren’t.
awards.distinguished_flying_medal_dfm: Courage and grit from an airman who kept flying. Earned the hard way, one operation after another.
awards.distinguished_service_order_dso: Leadership under fire, not just bravery. You kept men fighting when the odds went ugly.
awards.mentioned_in_despatches: Your name made it into the official reports. Quiet recognition for work done when it was most dangerous.
awards.raf_pilots_badge: Your wings are sewn on, and your life is scheduled around sorties. Welcome to the line.
awards.second_bar_to_the_dfc: Almost unheard of. You’ve repeatedly done what shouldn’t be survivable.
awards.second_bar_to_the_dfm: Rare repeat recognition for relentless operations. You’re becoming the kind of flyer the squadron leans on.
awards.second_bar_to_the_dso: Exceptionally rare and hard-won. You’ve led through repeated crisis and come out standing.
awards.second_wound_stripe: Hit again, still flying. Survival isn’t luck anymore—it’s endurance.
awards.third_wound_stripe: Three wounds and still on the roster. The squadron sees you and knows what it costs.
awards.victoria_cross_vc: The highest kind of courage—beyond orders, beyond reason. A moment that becomes history.
awards.wound_stripe: Proof the war reached you personally. The body keeps the receipt.
awards.air_force_medal: Steady hands and quiet courage in the air. You’ve proven yourself where discipline matters more than noise.
awards.bar_to_the_air_force_medal: More sorties, more pressure, the same standard held. The ribbon grows because you didn’t lower it.
awards.second_bar_to_the_air_force_medal: Sustained grit at operational height. Not a single act—but a pattern of resolve.
awards.air_force_cross: Leadership and nerve in the air. Responsibility now sits heavier, and you’ve shown you can carry it.
awards.bar_to_the_air_force_cross: Further distinction under command. The weight of decisions grows, and so does trust in your judgment.
awards.second_bar_to_the_air_force_cross: Repeated proof at the sharp end. Authority tested in fire—and held.
awards.third_bar_to_the_distinguished_service_o: A third bar to the DSO. Three separate recognitions, each requiring a standard most officers never meet once. The ribbon has grown; so has what's expected of you.
awards.france_and_germany_star: The final campaign. From Normandy to the Reich—you were flying when the war in Western Europe reached its conclusion. The star marks a road that ended in German airspace.

ranks.air_commodore: You direct whole air battles from reports and maps. If you fly, it’s exceptional—and everyone notices.
ranks.air_vice_marshal: The air war runs through your desk and into the sky. Flight is rare; command is relentless.
ranks.flight_lieutenant: You balance duty rosters and deadly skies. You still fly—because you won’t ask men to do what you won’t.
ranks.flight_sergeant: You’ve learned the sound of trouble before you see it. In the air, you’re steady—because panic kills.
ranks.flying_officer: You can lead a section and make it stick. When the radio goes quiet, your decisions speak loudest.
ranks.group_captain: A commander with a pilot’s instincts and a strategist’s burden. You fly rarely now, but you never stop listening to the engines.
ranks.pilot_officer: Commissioned, but still proving yourself every sortie. The squadron judges you by the way you hold formation under fire.
ranks.sergeant: Fresh wings, cold cockpit, and the Channel wind cutting through everything. Stay with your leader and keep your eyes moving.
ranks.squadron_leader: The squadron’s tempo is yours to set: push too hard and you break it. You fly when the moment needs a steady hand.
ranks.warrant_officer: A hard veteran in a soft uniform. You fly like you’ve paid for every lesson—and you have.
ranks.wing_commander: You command wings and you feel every loss. You go up sometimes—enough to keep the war honest.
ranks.corporal: Two chevrons and a small section depending on you. The RAF runs on men who keep it together at this level. Be that man.
ranks.air_marshal: You think in air campaigns, not sorties. Resources, strategy, and politics at the highest level. You may still fly—but the war moves through your decisions first.
ranks.air_chief_marshal: The peak of operational rank. What you decide shapes the shape of the air war. Every RAF wing in the theatre answers, ultimately, to a chain that ends here.

awards.front_flying_clasp_fighters_bronze: You’ve logged enough combat sorties to know the routine is deadly. The front doesn’t care how brave you feel.
awards.front_flying_clasp_fighters_gold: Heavy operational time at the sharp end. You’ve lived where the sky is full of fire.
awards.front_flying_clasp_fighters_silver: A long run of sorties under pressure. You’ve outlasted luck and learned discipline.
awards.german_cross_in_gold: Sustained combat success, the long grind turned into metal. You’ve been tested—repeatedly—and held.
awards.gold_with_pendant: An extreme tally of frontline sorties. You’ve been to war so often it feels like home—and that’s the danger.
awards.honor_goblet: A Luftwaffe trophy for men who fly beyond “enough.” It’s handed to those who keep coming back with victories and scars.
awards.iron_cross_1st_class: You didn’t just survive; you delivered results. The unit knows you’re the one to call when it’s hot.
awards.iron_cross_2nd_class: A first hard mark of combat service. Not glory—just proof you were there when it counted.
awards.knights_cross_of_the_iron_cross: A high honor for frontline achievement. You’ve made a name for yourself where it matters most.
awards.pilots_badge: You’ve earned the right to wear wings—and to be sent back up tomorrow. Training is over; the war starts now.
awards.with_golden_oak_leaves_swords_and_diamon: The top shelf, almost unheard of. You’ve become a symbol—and symbols still bleed.
awards.with_oak_leaves: More proof, more pressure. They expect miracles now—and they write your name in bigger letters.
awards.with_oak_leaves_and_swords: A mark for relentless frontline achievement. You’re not just fighting—you’re shaping the fight.
awards.with_oak_leaves_swords_and_diamonds: Rare, heavy, and impossible to ignore. Your record is legend; your risk stays real.
awards.wound_badge_in_black: First blood paid to the front. You came back—this time.
awards.wound_badge_in_gold: You’ve been hit again and again and kept returning. The badge shines; the damage doesn’t.
awards.wound_badge_in_silver: More wounds, fewer illusions. You’re still flying, but you’ve started counting what it costs.
awards.luftwaffe_honor_roll_clasp: Your name is no longer just on a roster—it stands in the Honor Roll. Recognition earned the hard way, through repeated proof at the front. It’s not applause; it’s expectation.

ranks.feldwebel: You’ve seen flak and fighters up close and you don’t flinch. Men follow your turns because they’ve learned you bring them home.
ranks.generalleutnant: The war looks different from this altitude—briefings, orders, consequences. You earned wings once; now you carry a theater.
ranks.generalmajor: You move squadrons like chess pieces and count fuel like blood. Flight time is rare; responsibility is constant.
ranks.hauptmann: Command and combat collide: paperwork at dawn, engine heat by noon. You fly when it matters and your name rides every outcome.
ranks.leutnant: Now you carry a commission and the weight that comes with it. You still fly the same sky, just with more eyes depending on you.
ranks.major: Your map table is larger than your cockpit time now. When you do fly, it’s because the mission can’t afford mistakes.
ranks.oberfeldwebel: Veteran hands, tired eyes—still climbing into the cockpit. You lead by example and the rookies copy everything you do.
ranks.oberleutnant: You lead flights into weather, flak, and bad odds. The Staffel watches how you handle the first burst and the last decision.
ranks.oberst: A commander with a pilot’s past and a war on his desk. If you take off, it’s for a reason everyone remembers.
ranks.oberstleutnant: You keep the unit running and the losses bear your signature. You fly rarely—usually to see the front with your own eyes.
ranks.unteroffizier: New to the line, you fly tight on a leader’s wing and learn fast or die fast. Your logbook fills one sortie at a time.
ranks.gefreiter: Your first stripe in a war that doesn't slow down for paperwork. You've earned enough trust for a chevron; now earn enough to keep it.
ranks.fhj_oberfeldwebel: Officer candidate with NCO rank—still waiting on the commission while flying like it's already yours. The paperwork will catch up. Keep performing.
ranks.general_der_jagdflieger: You direct the entire fighter arm. Operational priorities, unit dispositions, doctrine under fire—these are your instruments now. The sky belongs to the men you send into it.

awards.15_combat_sorties_bonus_2000_rubles: You’ve kept flying while others vanish. The state notices endurance.
awards.25_combat_sorties_bonus_3000_rubles: A real milestone at the front. You’ve stacked sorties like cordwood and kept moving.
awards.40_combat_sorties_bonus_5000_rubles: Heavy operational time—hard-earned and rarely clean. You’ve stayed in the fight long enough to be feared.
awards.5_combat_sorties_bonus_1500_rubles: A small reward for staying on the roster. The money is nice; the survival is the real prize.
awards.aviation_badge: You’re marked as aircrew now. The front will use you until the machine or the man breaks.
awards.hero_of_the_soviet_union: The highest title—heroism carved into the record. It doesn’t make the next sortie easier.
awards.hero_of_the_soviet_union_2nd_awarding: A rare second title for extraordinary repeat heroism. Even comrades look twice when your name is read.
awards.hero_of_the_soviet_union_3rd_awarding: Almost legendary. You’re a symbol now—and symbols are still sent into combat.
awards.medal_for_battle_merit: Solid service under fire. You did the work, took the risk, and brought results back.
awards.medal_for_courage: Personal bravery, close and undeniable. You held your nerve when the sky turned violent.
awards.order_of_alexander_nevsky: For leaders who win while outnumbered and under fire. A commander’s award, earned in the air.
awards.order_of_lenin: One of the highest honors, often paired with major heroism. A decoration that carries political weight and frontline respect.
awards.order_of_lenin_2nd_awarding: They’re elevating you again for continued distinction. Your war record is becoming impossible to ignore.
awards.order_of_lenin_3rd_awarding: A third time is exceptional. It marks a sustained level of achievement few ever reach.
awards.order_of_suvorov_3rd_class: Recognition for effective command and successful operations. You made plans work in a world that hates plans.
awards.order_of_the_patriotic_war_1st_class: A higher grade for standout performance in battle. Your name is being noticed beyond the regiment.
awards.order_of_the_patriotic_war_2nd_class: Combat merit that mattered to the Motherland. Earned in the grind, not the parade.
awards.order_of_the_red_banner: A major mark of courage and achievement. The kind of ribbon earned only at the sharp end.
awards.order_of_the_red_banner_2nd_awarding: They say you’ve done it again. Results repeated, losses endured, mission accomplished.
awards.order_of_the_red_banner_3rd_awarding: A third award speaks of a brutal record. You’ve fought hard, long, and successfully.
awards.order_of_the_red_star: A serious combat award for real results. Not for talk—only for what you did at the front.
awards.order_of_the_red_star_2nd_awarding: They’re recognizing you again. Same war, higher stakes, more proof you’re still delivering.
awards.order_of_the_red_star_3rd_awarding: A third time is no accident. You’ve made a career out of surviving—and winning.
awards.red_wound_stripe: You were wounded and still came back. The stripe is simple; the story isn’t.
awards.yellow_wound_stripe: Another mark of injury carried forward. You flew hurt, landed alive, and returned to duty.
awards.aircraft_kill_bonus_1000_rubles: The state pays for kills. One thousand rubles confirms that you fired, connected, and removed an aircraft from the enemy's count.
awards.fighter_kill_bonus_1000_rubles: Fighter downed. The threat is gone and the payment follows. A thousand rubles for a kill that may have saved a wingman.
awards.transport_plane_kill_bonus_1500_rubles: A transport removed from the supply equation. Fifteen hundred rubles for cutting a logistics thread the enemy was counting on.
awards.bomber_kill_bonus_1500_rubles: Bomber down before it reached the target. Fifteen hundred rubles for the mission it never completed.
awards.bomber_kill_bonus_2000_rubles: Another bomber removed from the enemy's order of battle. The bonus reflects the threat level. Two thousand rubles for keeping what lies below intact.
awards.small_ship_kill_bonus_1000_rubles: A small vessel put out of action. The bonus is modest; the result—one fewer enemy asset on the water—is not.
awards.transport_ship_kill_bonus_3000_rubles: A transport ship is not just a target—it is a supply chain. Three thousand rubles for stopping what it was carrying from arriving.
awards.destroyer_or_submarine_kill_bonus_10000_: A warship of substance—destroyer or submarine. Ten thousand rubles because the threat to friendly forces and supply lines was correspondingly serious. It won't be on the water again.
awards.medal_for_the_defense_of_moscow: Moscow itself was in the balance. You flew above a city that couldn't afford to fall, and it didn't. This medal records the battle that kept the war alive.
awards.medal_for_the_defense_of_stalingrad: Stalingrad—the battle that broke the Wehrmacht's strategic momentum. You were in the air above the city while it absorbed the worst the enemy could send. The medal marks a moment that changed the entire war.
awards.medal_for_the_defense_of_the_caucasus: The Caucasus campaign: oil, mountain passes, and the edge of a disaster that was turned back. You flew in the battles that kept the fuel and the southern flank out of enemy hands.

ranks.captain: You command and you still fly hard. The best orders are the ones you’ve tested in your own cockpit.
ranks.colonel: You carry an air regiment’s fate in your notes and your voice. Flying is occasional; responsibility never is.
ranks.junior_lieutenant: You’ve got a commission and a rifleman’s war in the air. Lead tight, strike fast, and don’t linger.
ranks.lieutenant: You’re trusted to bring a pair home and still finish the job. The sky is crowded and mercy is scarce.
ranks.lieutenant_general: The front is vast, the demands endless. You’re a pilot by training, a commander by necessity.
ranks.major: You fly less, plan more, and sleep even less. When you do climb out, it’s for missions that must succeed.
ranks.major_general: You command formations and watch losses like a ledger of steel. If you fly, it’s exceptional—and never for sport.
ranks.senior_lieutenant: You lead sorties into flak and weather like it’s routine. Your squadron runs on discipline and stubbornness.
ranks.senior_sergeant: You’ve survived enough to teach others how to. The new men watch your hands more than they hear your words.
ranks.sergeant: A frontline pilot with little margin and no illusions. You fly, you fight, you hope the engine holds.
ranks.sub_colonel: Command pulls you away from the line, but you return when it matters. A rare sortie, a familiar smell of fuel and frost.
ranks.efreitor: One step above the bottom. The stripe is small; the expectations just got larger. You show up, you hold the line, you don't cost anyone extra effort. That's the job.
ranks.mladshiy_serzhant: Junior sergeant. The title is small but the role is real. Someone is now watching how you handle pressure. Don't let them down.
ranks.general_polkovnik: Command at the scale of armies. You coordinate fronts, allocate air armies, and answer to the Stavka. The individual aircraft are abstractions; you move the whole instrument of air power.

awards.air_medal: Meritorious flying under combat conditions. It’s the war’s way of saying you kept delivering.
awards.air_medal_plus_one_oak_leaf_cluster: You’ve earned it again. Same sky, more missions, more proof.
awards.air_medal_plus_three_oak_leaf_clusters: Repeated awards for repeated sorties. The ribbon stack grows as the risks don’t stop.
awards.air_medal_plus_two_oak_leaf_clusters: A steady record of combat flying. You’re becoming a veteran by accumulation.
awards.bronze_star_medal: Combat merit and hard service recognized. Not glamorous—just earned where it’s dangerous.
awards.bronze_star_plus_one_oak_leaf_cluster: Another round of meritorious service under fire. They’re counting what you’ve carried.
awards.bronze_star_plus_two_oak_leaf_clusters: A third recognition for staying effective in the long grind. You’ve become dependable the hard way.
awards.dfc_plus_four_oak_leaf_clusters: More than most ever see in a lifetime. It means you keep walking into the worst and coming out.
awards.dfc_plus_one_oak_leaf_cluster: You’ve done it again—another exceptional mission, another line in the record.
awards.dfc_plus_one_silver_oak_leaf_cluster: A higher-count mark of repeat awards. You’ve stacked extraordinary sorties like normal work.
awards.dfc_plus_three_oak_leaf_clusters: Repeated extraordinary performance. Your reputation is built on missions that should’ve gone wrong.
awards.dfc_plus_two_oak_leaf_clusters: A sustained pattern of standout flying. The enemy isn’t the only thing watching you now.
awards.distinguished_flying_cross: Heroism or extraordinary achievement in the air. The kind of sortie people talk about afterward.
awards.distinguished_service_cross: Extraordinary heroism in combat. The kind of action that becomes a unit legend.
awards.dsc_plus_four_oak_leaf_clusters: Almost unheard of. You’ve done the impossible too many times to count.
awards.dsc_plus_one_oak_leaf_cluster: A second time for extreme heroism. That’s not luck—that’s a pattern of risk.
awards.dsc_plus_three_oak_leaf_clusters: Repeated actions at the edge of survivability. Your record reads like a warning label.
awards.dsc_plus_two_oak_leaf_clusters: A third award for extraordinary heroism. Few ever reach this—and fewer live through it.
awards.legion_of_merit: Outstanding service over time, beyond a single fight. You’ve carried the war on your shoulders and kept it moving.
awards.medal_of_honor: Valor above and beyond—an act that rewrites what “duty” means. The highest recognition for the darkest moment.
awards.medal_of_honor_plus_one_oak_leaf_cluster: A second Medal of Honor is nearly unimaginable. It means you faced that line twice and crossed it.
awards.pilots_badge: Your wings say you’re rated and ready. Now the mission board tells you where you’ll bleed for them.
awards.purple_heart: You were hit by the enemy and paid in blood. The medal is quiet; the memory isn’t.
awards.purple_heart_plus_one_oak_leaf_cluster: Wounded again. You carry the damage and keep flying anyway.
awards.purple_heart_plus_two_oak_leaf_clusters: Three wounds and still operational. The body keeps score even if the medal does not.
awards.silver_star_medal: Gallantry in action. A moment of courage that refused to break.
awards.silver_star_plus_one_oak_leaf_cluster: Again, you stood when others might not. Repeated bravery under fire.
awards.silver_star_plus_two_oak_leaf_clusters: A third gallantry award is a hard statement. You don’t just survive trouble—you face it.
awards.air_medal_plus_four_oak_leaf_clusters: Five awards for aerial achievement under combat conditions. The clusters are the war's arithmetic: each one is more sorties, more exposure, more of the same sky that doesn't get any safer.
awards.air_medal_plus_one_silver_leaf_cluster: A silver oak leaf cluster in lieu of five additional awards. The ribbon can't keep up with the missions. The flying kept going anyway.
awards.european_african_middle_eastern_campaign: Across the theaters that turned the war. North Africa, the Mediterranean, the approaches to Europe—you were there while the strategic balance shifted. The medal marks the geography of a victory that wasn't guaranteed.

ranks.1st_lieutenant: You’ve seen enough to stop pretending it’s easy. Now you lead flights and carry men through bad weather and worse skies.
ranks.2nd_lieutenant: Brand-new bars, same flak and same fear. Your lead is light, but the war doesn’t care.
ranks.brigadier_general: You shape operations across units and bases. If you take the air, it’s a statement—and a risk you don’t take lightly.
ranks.captain: You’re a leader and a target both. You still fly—because credibility is earned at altitude.
ranks.chief_warrant_officer: You’re the quiet expert—engines, tactics, nerves of steel. When it gets ugly, they want you in the formation.
ranks.colonel: You command from the top but you’ve flown the hard miles. Flight is rare—your war is coordination and consequence.
ranks.first_sergeant: You keep the unit stitched together when the mission tears it apart. If you fly, it’s to share the risk, not the glory.
ranks.flight_officer: You’re rated to fly and thrown into the grinder. Learn fast, hit hard, and don’t waste luck.
ranks.lt_colonel: Bigger command, fewer takeoffs. When you do fly, it’s to see the truth beyond the paperwork.
ranks.major: Plans, briefings, and harder calls than trigger pulls. You fly selectively now, usually when the mission needs a proven hand.
ranks.major_general: Strategy, logistics, and the weight of whole formations. Your flying days are mostly memory, but the sky is still yours.
ranks.staff_sergeant: Three up, two down. You are the institutional memory of your unit and the backbone of its discipline. Officers set direction; you make it work.
ranks.technical_sergeant: Technical Sergeant. You keep the machines running and the crews honest. What you know about this aircraft is what keeps it flying and the men in it alive.
ranks.lieutenant_general: Three stars. You run air campaigns across theaters and shape the strategy that aircrew execute at altitude. The men at the sharp end are distant—but every decision you make echoes in the sky over them.
